description: Labelled, fully-offline regression evaluation: process() resolves fixture-backed strong identifiers, emits no result for the bundled ambiguous or non-existent inputs, and flags input text that contradicts the resolved DOI metadata.

cases.note: Real Crossref DOI resolves to a source-resolved entry.
Real arXiv identifier resolves via the arXiv API.
Real PMID resolves via PubMed then Crossref enrichment.
Real GitHub repository URL resolves to software metadata.
Real Zenodo DOI resolves via the Zenodo API.
Real DataCite-registered DOI resolves via the DataCite fallback.

cases.input: a deep learning paper about attention and transformers
cases.note: Plain-text title carries no strong identifier; process() must not auto-emit a source-resolved entry (this is what `onecite suggest` is for).

cases.input: Smith et al., neural networks for vision, 2019
cases.note: Partial author/year snippet is not a strong identifier and must stay unresolved.
Syntactically valid but non-existent DOI (the kind an LLM may hallucinate) is rejected, never fabricated into an entry.
Plausible-looking fabricated DOI returns 404 from both Crossref and DataCite and is rejected.

cases.input: Attention Is All You Need. Vaswani, A. et al. (2017). doi:10.1038/nature14236
cases.note: A real DOI is paired with a different paper's title. The supplied DOI resolves to the DQN paper, but the mismatch must be flagged for review rather than silently presented as clean source-resolved output.
